title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
description: Ten documented Carleton spaces for solo work, collaboration, writing support, quantitative work, or laptop-based study; confirm local schedules before visiting.

cards.title: Settle Into Gould Library
cards.subtitle: Hundreds of seats plus research and computing resources
cards.notes: Choose Gould when you need books, public computers, or room to shift between individual work and a group session under one roof.
cards.short_summary: Carleton’s principal library combines extensive collections with 450 documented study spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Carleton’s 2023–24 catalog documents 450 study spaces, 52 public-access computers, a computer lab, and 18 group study rooms in Gould Library.
cards.access_notes: Library access and individual service availability may vary by date; consult current Carleton library information before visiting.

cards.title: Bring the Project to a Group Room
cards.subtitle: Eighteen enclosed collaboration spaces in Gould Library
cards.notes: Use a group room for discussion-heavy work, then verify any current booking or occupancy rules with the library before meeting.
cards.short_summary: A set of enclosed rooms gives collaborative work a defined home inside Gould.
cards.evidence_claim: Carleton’s 2023–24 catalog states that Gould Library contains 18 group study rooms.
cards.access_notes: The cited catalog confirms the rooms but does not state current reservation rules; verify availability with Gould Library.

cards.title: Use the Open Computer Lab Window
cards.subtitle: Third-floor library classroom with computers
cards.notes: Check the room schedule first, then use 306 for computer-based work only when no library instruction session occupies the space.
cards.short_summary: Room 306 changes from an instruction classroom to an open computer lab when unscheduled.
cards.evidence_claim: Gould Library’s official tour identifies Room 306 as a third-floor library classroom and computer lab that is open when not in use.
cards.source_title: Classrooms and Computer Labs — Library Tour
cards.access_notes: Open as a computer lab only when the room is not being used for library instruction; check the posted schedule.

cards.title: Work Through a Draft at the Writing Center
cards.subtitle: Writing support located inside Gould Library
cards.notes: Bring a prompt, outline, or draft and use this library-based center when the useful next step is focused writing support.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated academic-support destination for developing written work inside the library.
cards.evidence_claim: Carleton’s 2023–24 catalog states that the Writing Center and Academic Support are located in Gould Library.
cards.access_notes: The catalog confirms the location but not current consultation hours or appointment rules; check Academic Support before visiting.

cards.title: Take Quantitative Work to the QRC
cards.subtitle: Dedicated quantitative-support center in Gould Library
cards.notes: Bring the problem set and identify the sticking point before arriving; confirm current staffing and session arrangements in advance.
cards.short_summary: A library-based destination centered on quantitative coursework and academic support.
cards.evidence_claim: Carleton’s 2023–24 catalog identifies the Quantitative Resource Center as a facility located in Gould Library.
cards.access_notes: The cited catalog does not provide current staffing hours, eligibility, or appointment requirements; verify with Academic Support.

cards.title: Spread Out in Anderson’s Study Lounges
cards.subtitle: Small collaboration spaces embedded in the science building
cards.notes: Use these soft-seating areas for science review or a compact team session while respecting nearby classes, labs, and meetings.
cards.short_summary: Purpose-planned lounges place informal individual and collaborative work inside Anderson Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Carleton describes Anderson Hall as containing strategically placed small study lounges and meeting spaces intended for informal learning and teamwork.
cards.access_notes: The source confirms the lounges but gives no current public-access rules; building and room access may follow campus schedules.

cards.title: Use the Atrium Between Commitments
cards.subtitle: Named central space in Anderson Hall
cards.notes: Choose the atrium for portable work between nearby classes, and relocate if a scheduled gathering needs the shared space.
cards.short_summary: A named Anderson Hall atrium suited to a short, flexible laptop or reading session.
cards.evidence_claim: Carleton’s official 2024 campus map identifies Daugherty Atrium as a named space in Anderson Hall.
cards.access_notes: The campus map confirms the place but not study permission, seating, or event schedules; use only while normally open and available.

cards.title: Take a Reading Session to the Commons
cards.subtitle: Named gathering space in the Weitz Center for Creativity
cards.notes: Bring self-contained reading or laptop work to this shared commons, and check for events before planning a longer session.
cards.short_summary: A documented commons inside Weitz offers an alternative to classroom-style surroundings.
cards.evidence_claim: Carleton’s official 2024 campus map lists the Class of 1980 Commons as an event and exhibition space in the Weitz Center.
cards.access_notes: This is a shared event space, not a documented reservable study room; confirm that it is open and unscheduled before settling in.

cards.title: Keep the Work Portable in Great Space
cards.subtitle: Large interior court in Sayles-Hill Campus Center
cards.notes: Use a compact setup that can move easily, since this central campus-center court also supports activities and scheduled events.
cards.short_summary: Sayles-Hill’s named interior court provides a central shared setting for brief work sessions.
cards.evidence_claim: Carleton’s campus history describes Great Space as a large interior court created in Sayles-Hill, and the current campus map still names it there.
cards.access_notes: Great Space is a multipurpose campus-center area; check current building access and avoid occupying it during scheduled activities.

cards.title: Focus Language Work at the Language Center
cards.subtitle: Academic language facility in the Language and Dining Center
cards.notes: Bring listening, speaking, or text-based language work here, and confirm which facilities are available outside scheduled classes.
cards.short_summary: A named academic center gives language-focused work a clear campus destination.
cards.evidence_claim: Carleton’s official 2024 campus map locates the Language Center in the Language and Dining Center.
cards.access_notes: The map establishes the location but not current equipment access, room availability, or operating hours; verify with the center.
